note_text:
67-year-old male presents for discussion of management of newly diagnosed prostate adenocarcinoma. PSA 8.2 ng/mL. Prostate biopsy showed Gleason 4+3=7 adenocarcinoma involving 3 of 12 cores, with maximum linear tumor extent 6 mm in the dominant core. Staging workup including bone scan and pelvic CT/MRI revealed multiple sclerotic lesions in the lumbar spine and pelvis, and enlarged pelvic and retroperitoneal lymph nodes concerning for nodal and osseous metastatic disease. Confirmatory MRI of the spine demonstrates diffuse marrow replacement consistent with metastatic involvement.

Patient is otherwise in good health, ECOG 0, with no significant comorbidities and estimated life expectancy well over 10 years based on age and overall functional status. He has not received any prior pelvic radiation or androgen deprivation therapy; the biopsy tissue described above was obtained prior to any treatment.

Given the biopsy specimen has adequate tumor volume (>0.5 mm linear extent) in FFPE tissue, we discussed the possibility of sending the specimen for genomic classifier testing to help refine risk stratification and guide decision-making between active surveillance, definitive local therapy, or systemic therapy per current guideline-based treatment pathways. However, given the imaging findings strongly suggestive of metastatic spread to bone and lymph nodes, this case represents metastatic rather than localized or biochemically recurrent disease. We will proceed with confirmatory bone biopsy and initiate systemic therapy per medical oncology; genomic classifier assay is not indicated at this time given documented metastatic disease. Patient will continue to be followed with serial PSA and imaging per standard of care surveillance protocol, and treatment decisions will be individualized in coordination with medical oncology and radiation oncology according to guideline recommendations once metastatic workup is finalized.
